title: Enforce live booking authorization and customer scope across logistics lifecycle
description: Stage3 core inventory closure. Use genuine authenticated existing ERP permissions; no new user grants or anonymous/admin fallback. Retain inventory source document audit and original failed logs. Run relevant unit tests and safe Release build/full unit suite. Real SQL must target exact (localdb)\NEWERP_AutoAcceptance with IntegratedSecurity and a new GUID-owned NEWERP_AUTOTEST database; reject existing/wrong target before access, never drop/reset or read production settings. Include two independent connection race tests where applicable. Build completion never implies stage acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: An existing booking operator must resolve current enabled nondeleted user and real booking menu on every list/detail/timeline/options/create/update/submit/approve/cancel/delete route before counts, number generation, source reads or mutation. Reuse SalespersonDataScopeService and authoritative CustomerId; database-side scope precedes pagination/count. Restricted users can only read/write own-customer booking; missing identity, unmapped user or revoked menu fail closed, never global/admin fallback.

Validate required customer and optional supplier against enabled live masterdata before new/update/state-changing operations, preserve historical reads with explicit unavailable evidence. Edit cannot move a booking into another customer scope. Serialize booking state mutations under the ERP353 booking row lock; preserve preloading/loading cancellation protection, shipment fields and original audit. No grants, new schema or external operations. Verify actual controllers with real SQL own/foreign identities, disabled source, revocation, failed edit unchanged and concurrent state transitions.
